_comment: Every constant the selector obeys lives HERE, not scattered in code, so a
run's quotas are a versioned artifact that can be diffed and re-run.
Sources: docs/1M/T2_instructions.md Steps 6-13, gates G1-G20 in Step 15.
DENOMINATOR RULE (v1.1): every share below is a fraction of the ACTUAL
selected population, never of the requested target. The selector finds the
largest N for which a population of exactly N satisfies all of them, so a
larger --target can never buy a looser cap.

task._rule: q_t proportional to sqrt(N_t), clipped to [min_share_rich, max_share]; candidate-poor tasks kept in full. max_share is the TARGET, hard_ceiling is the never-exceed bound checked against the actual population (G8).

language._rule: Shares of the LANGUAGE-APPLICABLE population (everything except language-neutral). language_neutral_max_share is a share of the whole population.
language._supply_note: Adjusted from (0.64/0.22/0.13/0.01) after measurement. The pool's language-applicable mix is english 25.95% / multi 13.18% / non-english 12.52% / unknown 48.35% -- most English models simply never declare `language: en`, so an english-primary target of 64% was unreachable and produced a 16.7pp G14 deviation. These targets are the measured achievable split; the >=75% English floor is unchanged and still binds.

family_size._supply_note: Adjusted from (0.35/0.30/0.20/0.15) after measurement. The pool is large 35.73% / medium 5.47% / small 14.28% / singleton 44.52%: a 30% medium target against 5.47% supply is the 'unreasonable target' Step 8 says to adjust. These keep large families prioritized (35% > their 35.7% pool share is neutral, and they are also the ones the family cap throttles) and every non-singleton stratum above its pool share, while cutting singletons below theirs.

source_type._rule: official-quantized (first-party release) is NOT the same population as quantized-conversion (third-party repackaging); the 15% ceiling is on the third-party class.

score_weights._comment: Used only to ORDER candidates inside an eligible bucket. Hard quotas and caps always take precedence (Step 13).

axis_priority._comment: Weight on each axis' deficit when choosing which bucket to fill next.

feasible_search._comment: Binary search for the largest N with achieved(N) >= N. All caps are shares of N, so this is the exact feasible maximum under this config.
